Ah, you're absolutely right—thanks for the correction! 

`COUNT(email)` only counts non-NULL values in that column, so the 980 represents users with an email address. `COUNT(*)` counts all rows regardless of NULL values, which is why it returns the full 1000. So those 20 missing rows are users with NULL in the email column.

This is an important distinction when auditing data—if you need to know the total row count, `COUNT(*)` is what you want. If you're counting a specific column, you'll get a different result if that column has NULLs.
